system-design-001.base: Walk me through your latency budget. Where do you spend it?
variants: The product team says the homepage must render in 150 ms, including recommendations. How do you split that time across retrieval, ranking and feature lookup?
Your ranking model alone takes 120 ms of a 200 ms budget. Where do you look for savings?

system-design-001.base: Your model training takes 6 hours. How do you keep recommendations fresh without retraining constantly?
variants: A user just bought a tent. How do your recommendations reflect that within minutes when the model retrains nightly?
Retraining is expensive, but item popularity shifts within hours during sales. What can you update without retraining the full model?

system-design-001.base: How would you A/B test this system without a madhouse of feature flags?
variants: Three teams want to test ranking changes at the same time on the same page. How do you set that up?
How do you test a new candidate-retrieval model when the ranker downstream was trained on the old retrieval's output?

system-design-002.base: Users need forecasts updated daily. Do you batch or serve predictions on-demand?
variants: Most customers look at their forecast once a week, but a few check it hourly. How does that shape whether you precompute?
Forecasts take 2 seconds per customer to compute. Is on-demand serving still viable?

system-design-002.base: A customer's 90-day forecast suddenly drops 50%. Should you alert them? Why?
variants: A forecast drops sharply because one large invoice was paid early. Would an alert help the customer or confuse them?
What checks would you run before showing a customer a forecast that changed by more than 30% overnight?

system-design-002.base: How would you version your model changes without breaking live dashboards?
variants: A new model version changes every customer's forecast by about 5%. How do you roll it out without users thinking something broke?
Finance compares this month's dashboard with last month's export. How do you keep those comparable across model versions?

system-design-003.base: How do you prevent the system from becoming a dumping ground for half-baked ideas?
variants: Half the requests submitted last quarter never had a clear business owner. What do you change in intake?
How would you decide which requests get a data scientist's time first?

system-design-003.base: Teams want different SLOs (some want real-time, some want batch). How do you standardize without being rigid?
variants: One team needs predictions in 50 ms and another is fine with a nightly file. What do you standardize, and what do you leave flexible?
Every team asks for an exception to the platform's defaults. How do you decide which exceptions to support?

system-design-004.base: How do you assign users to variants so that assignment is stable and independent across experiments?
variants: A user is in experiment A and starts experiment B tomorrow. How do you make sure B's assignment doesn't depend on A's?
Users log in on several devices. How do you keep them in the same variant?

system-design-004.base: Your 50/50 split shows 52/48 in the data. What does it mean and what do you do?
variants: Your 50/50 test shows 50.8% versus 49.2% with a million users. Is that a sample ratio mismatch?
The treatment arm has fewer users than expected only on mobile. What would you investigate?

system-design-004.base: How do you prevent two overlapping experiments from interfering with each other?
variants: The pricing team and the checkout team both want to run tests on the checkout page this month. How do you set it up?
How would you detect whether two simultaneous experiments interact?

system-design-005.base: How fresh do the features actually need to be, and who decides that?
variants: The fraud team says they need real-time features. How do you find out how fresh they really need to be?
What would it cost the business if a feature were 1 hour old instead of 1 second old? How would you estimate that?

system-design-005.base: How do you keep the batch and streaming versions of a feature consistent?
variants: The model was trained on features computed in a nightly batch, but in production they come from a stream. What can go wrong?
How would you test that the batch and streaming versions of 'transactions in the last hour' give the same values?

system-design-005.base: How do you handle late-arriving events in a streaming pipeline?
variants: Mobile events can arrive 20 minutes late. How does that affect a streaming 'clicks in the last 5 minutes' feature?
What is the difference between event time and processing time, and which should a window use?

system-design-006.base: The decision has to be made in under 100 milliseconds. How does that shape the design?
variants: Your best fraud features need a database query that takes 300 ms. How do you use them within a 100 ms decision?
Which features can you precompute, and which must be computed at transaction time?

system-design-006.base: Fraudsters adapt to your model. How does that change how you monitor and retrain?
variants: Fraud losses were stable for months, then tripled in one week while model scores looked normal. What happened, and how do you respond?
How would you detect that fraudsters are probing your model with small test transactions?

system-design-006.base: A false positive blocks a legitimate customer at checkout. How do you account for that?
variants: Blocking a legitimate $2,000 purchase loses the sale and possibly the customer. How does that factor into the decision rule?
Instead of approve or decline, what other actions could the system take for borderline cases?

system-design-007.base: Would you build one model or twenty? How do you decide?
variants: Five units have three years of history and the rest have under a year. One model or several?
What would a global model with a unit feature give you that twenty separate models wouldn't?

system-design-007.base: How do you keep unit forecasts consistent with the company total?
variants: The CFO looks only at the company total, while unit heads look at their own numbers. How do you keep both views consistent?
Unit forecasts add up to 8% more than the company forecast. Which do you adjust?

system-design-007.base: How would the finance team use and challenge the forecast?
variants: A unit head says the forecast is too low because a big contract is about to close. How does the system take in that knowledge?
What would you show finance so they can see why the forecast moved this week?

system-design-011.base: How do you detect and handle a schema change at one source?
variants: One source renamed a column overnight and your pipeline loaded NULLs for a whole day. How should the system have caught it?
How would you agree a data contract with five source teams who all change things on their own schedule?

system-design-011.base: What happens when a run fails halfway?
variants: The pipeline loaded three of five sources before failing. What happens when you rerun it?
How do you make the daily load safe to run twice?

system-design-011.base: How do you reconcile the five sources to the same numbers?
variants: Total transaction value differs by 2% between your warehouse and the source systems. How do you track down the gap?
Which reconciliation checks would you run every day, and which weekly?

system-design-012.base: How do you handle seasonality and holidays?
variants: Sales always drop 40% on public holidays. How do you stop the system alerting every time?
A metric has a strong weekly cycle and a slow upward trend. What baseline would you compare against?

system-design-012.base: How do you keep false alarms down?
variants: Analysts received 60 alerts last week and acted on 3. What do you change?
How would you use analysts' responses to alerts to improve the system over time?

system-design-012.base: What would you show alongside an alert?
variants: An alert says revenue is down 12% today. What context should come with it so an analyst can act quickly?
How would you point analysts toward which segment or region caused an anomaly?

system-design-013.base: How do you chunk and index the documents?
variants: Some documents are 300-page PDFs and others are one-line tickets. How do you chunk them?
What metadata would you store with each chunk, and why?

system-design-013.base: When does pure vector search fail, and what do you add?
variants: A user searches for an exact error code and vector search returns loosely related documents. What do you add?
Searches for product names and acronyms perform poorly. Why might embeddings struggle with them?
An employee searches and sees a snippet from a document they aren't allowed to open. Where did the design go wrong?
Permissions change daily. How do you keep the search index in sync?

system-design-014.base: How do you make the forecast respond to assumptions the model has never seen?
variants: A user asks what happens if prices rise 15%, but prices have never moved more than 3% in your history. How does the tool answer?
Which parts of the scenario should come from the model and which from explicit business rules?
How would you show the range of outcomes for a scenario, not just one line?
Users compare two scenarios whose difference is smaller than the forecast's uncertainty. What do you show them?

system-design-014.base: How do you make sure users don't treat scenarios as predictions?
variants: A scenario showing 20% growth ends up in a board deck as the forecast. How could the tool have prevented that?
How would you label scenario outputs so they aren't mistaken for the official forecast?

system-design-008.base: How do you define churn so the label is usable?
variants: Customers on annual contracts can only churn at renewal. How do you define the label for them?
Should a customer who downgrades to the free plan count as churned? How do you decide?

system-design-008.base: How do you turn scores into actions the team can take?
variants: The team can contact 200 customers a week, but the model flags 1,500 as high risk. How do you prioritize?
Some high-risk customers can't be saved by any offer the team has. How should that affect the list?

system-design-008.base: How do you measure whether the interventions actually helped?
variants: Retention went up after launch. How do you know the interventions caused it?
How would you set up a holdout group, and how would you explain the need for it to the retention team?

system-design-009.base: How do you produce reasons for a decision that a customer can understand?
variants: A customer is declined and asks why. How do you turn SHAP values into a reason they can act on?
Two features with similar effects both appear in the explanation. Which do you show the customer?

system-design-009.base: How do you monitor the system for unfair outcomes?
variants: Approval rates differ by 10 points between two age groups. How do you decide whether that's a problem?
Which fairness metrics would you monitor, and why can't you satisfy all of them at once?

system-design-009.base: How do you approve and record a model change?
variants: A regulator asks which model version decided a loan 18 months ago and why. What does your system need to have stored?
Who signs off on a new model version, and what evidence do they need?

system-design-010.base: Where do metric definitions live, and who can change them?
variants: Marketing and finance both claim ownership of the 'active user' definition. How do you resolve it?
Where would you store metric definitions so analysts actually use them?

system-design-010.base: How do you handle a definition that needs to change?
variants: The business decides 'active user' should now exclude free-trial users. How do you roll that change out?
Historical dashboards will shift when a definition changes. How do you handle that?

system-design-010.base: How do you check that dashboards match the layer?
variants: A team's dashboard shows revenue 3% higher than the metrics layer. How would you catch that automatically?
What tests would you run on the metrics layer itself?
